name: Old Gippstown

facts.claim: Open-air museum and reconstructed pioneer township in Moe, Victoria
Located at 211 Lloyd Street, Moe
Open Wednesday to Sunday

access_note: Open Wed-Sun only; cafe temporarily closed from 24 Aug 2026

name: Walhalla

facts.claim: Gold-mining town founded in late 1862, home to about 4,000 at its peak and about 20 permanent residents now
Long Tunnel Extended Gold Mine runs underground tours; adult $25 (excl. GST)
Walhalla Goldfields Railway, cemetery, post office museum and ghost tours are listed attractions
Walhalla Historic Area is a Parks Victoria-managed area

ticketUrl_note: Walhalla Heritage board site, title 'Visit Walhalla'; redirected from walhalla.org.au
access_note: Town is free to wander; mine tour (adult $25, tour basis) is an extra, not the spot price. Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee but not explicitly confirmed.

name: Baw Baw National Park

facts.claim: About 13,530 ha national park on the Victorian Alps/Gippsland boundary, about 120 km east of Melbourne
Covers much of the Baw Baw Plateau with snowgum forest and wildflowers in spring
Mushroom Rocks is a maze of giant granite tors on the Australian Alps Walking Track
Mount St Gwinear is a free-entry snow-play area in winter

ticketUrl_note: Parks Victoria page, title names the park
access_note: Victorian national parks charge no entry; page shows no fee. Consider costBasis 'park' with free:true per owner convention.

name: Mount Baw Baw

facts.claim: Alpine resort village at 1450 m amongst snow gum forest on the Baw Baw Plateau
Melbourne's closest ski and snow resort
Summer activities include hiking, mountain biking and walks
Summit on the Baw-Baw Plateau, Great Dividing Range, Gippsland

access_note: Resort entry free in green season; a winter resort entry fee probably applies (not found on page). Facilities closed in green season.
unresolved: winter resort entry fee not found

name: Toorongo Falls

facts.claim: Reserve protects Toorongo Falls and Amphitheatre Falls, about 6 km north-east of Noojee
Walk passes through tall, wet forest with several viewpoints of the falls and continues to Amphitheatre Falls
Main falls about 25 m high, with a viewing platform

ticketUrl_note: Victorian Government forests site (managing agency), 'No fees payable'; page title Toorongo Falls
